bug_semantics: A ZIP entry name controlled by an archive sender was concatenated directly to a temporary extraction-directory path and opened with FileOutputStream without normalization or a containment check. An entry such as ../../target therefore escaped the temporary directory, overwrote an arbitrary server-writable file, and was then passed to deletion cleanup. The vulnerable helper was reachable both from configured email-attachment unpacking and from MakeUnzipFileAction.
flaw_origin: Commit 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827 first added opt-in archive unpacking to EmailReceiver and introduced unpackZIPFile with ze.getName() flowing directly into new File(outputDirectory.getPath() + "/" + fileName) and FileOutputStream. Commit ce3cf594f118e720279abdb78116a597956bbe41 later added the same unsafe extraction mechanism to MakeUnzipFileAction; commit 4950d66839375b11a4706fe1b5bd5f28ec9abf17 was a refactor that centralized the already-vulnerable implementations in ZipUtils, not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827 shows author and committer Vandrouny <filipchyk.andrei@gmail.com>, the single subject '[server] Опция распаковки архивов при приёме почты', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailer/commit-object AI marker.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/lsfusion/platform/issues/1545 identifies ZipUtils.unpackFile, MakeUnzipFileAction, and EmailReceiver and describes remotely supplied archive names/symlinks escaping extraction to overwrite and delete files. `git log --all --reverse -S'ZipInputStream'` on historical server/src/main/java/lsfusion/server/mail/EmailReceiver.java identifies 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827 (2017-05-24) as the first EmailReceiver ZIP extractor; the equivalent search on historical fsl-server/src/main/java/lsfusion/erp/utils/utils/MakeUnzipFileActionProperty.java identifies later commit ce3cf594f118e720279abdb78116a597956bbe41 (2017-08-15). `git show 557102...` shows EmailReceiver.unpack dispatching .zip attachments to unpackZIPFile and the vulnerable sequence `String fileName = ze.getName(); outputFile = new File(outputDirectory.getPath() + "/" + fileName); new FileOutputStream(outputFile)` with no normalization/containment test. Direct parent-tree inspection at 6747b4ead5e8f26ccd36ecb33e77aa9ea9335fe1:server/src/main/java/lsfusion/server/mail/EmailReceiver.java shows the class ending after MultipartBody, with no unpack dispatcher, unpackZIPFile, ZipInputStream import, or archive-entry write path; the BIC diff adds all of them. `git show 4950d66839375b11a4706fe1b5bd5f28ec9abf17 --find-copies` identifies ZipUtils as a 52% copy from MakeUnzipFileAction and changes both MakeUnzipFileAction and EmailReceiver to call ZipUtils.unpackFile, proving that 4950d668... centralized rather than originated the flaw. Direct fix 1aefa1fd67bb644e6d4f5682051fc85b81048322 adds `if (!filePath.contains("../"))` around the ZIP write; release-line cherry-pick 547f9c92df24969fb34f6d7009bfeb3d7727c67a records its source as 1aefa1fd... and both commits have stable patch-id 4ba1c5411569c90ccac57099811a1285acbe05db. Version checks show the BIC is an ancestor of tags 6.0-beta2 and 6.1; tag 6.1's ZipUtils still writes filePath unchecked. Neither the direct fix nor the release cherry-pick is in 6.1, while 547f9c92... is an ancestor of tag 6.2 and tag 6.2 contains the traversal guard. Thus repository history and the first-party issue establish 6.1 as vulnerable and 6.2 as the first tagged patched boundary, despite the GHSA package metadata stating `<= 6.0-beta2` and leaving first_patched_version null. BIC commit-object evidence comes exclusively from `git cat-file -p 557102...`.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle begins with 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827, which made untrusted email archives executable through ZIP extraction and first wrote the unchecked entry-name-to-filesystem data flow. Its immediate parent directly lacks the entire extraction path. ce3cf594... subsequently introduced the same mechanism for the explicit unzip action, and 4950d668... later moved the two existing implementations into the advisory-named ZipUtils and routed both callers through it; selecting that refactor would violate the smallest-real-BIC rule. The direct security edit is 1aefa1fd..., while identical cherry-pick 547f9c92... is the commit that crosses the release boundary: 6.1 retains the unsafe flow and 6.2 has the guard. The BIC is a normal human-authored 2017 commit whose raw commit object contains no AI identity or trailer. Because AI attribution is judged only on that BIC, the result is NOT_AI.
